Tunafikiria nini tunaposikia neno ‘kanisa’? Tunaishi katika wakati ambao kuna makanisa mengi na anuwai. Ikiwa kanisa moja hakufaa, kuna mengine ya kuchagua. Wakati baadhi ya makanisa yanahimiza watu wao kuishi kwa ajili ya Mungu na wengine badala ya wao wenyewe, makanisa mengine yanatangaza injili inayosema pesa nyingi na maisha bora sasa ni matokeo ya kumfuata Kristo. Hata hivyo, bado kuna makanisa yanayojaribu kufuata kile Biblia inasema—Sola scriptura (maandiko peke yao). Kiafisi, makanisa ya Anabaptist yenye msimamo mkali huko Amerika yamejaribu kufanya kazi kwa mtindo huu. Lakini je, hilo linabadilika?

Tunaishi katika wakati ambapo mipaka inavuka, kuharibika, na kuchanganywa. Watu hawana uhakika ni nini ni kweli na ni nini si kweli. Leo, wanaume na wanawake kote ulimwenguni wanatafuta majibu na suluhisho, lakini wanapaswa kutafuta wapi?

Nilikuwa nikipiga gumzo na kijana mmoja ambaye alishuhudia kuwa alibadilishwa moyo akiwa mdogo. Alihudhuria kanisani kwa uaminifu na alionekana mwenye kipaji. Lakini kulikuwa na tatizo—aliacha kuchezea dhambi ambayo hakuweza kudhibiti. Wakati alipokuwa akipigana na Mungu na kuomba ushindi, alianza kusikia ujumbe unaorudiwa kutoka kwa Wakristo wengine wanaodai, “Hakuna mtu mkamilifu!” “Sote tuna matatizo.” “Kila mtu amekwenda dhambini!” Mwishowe, kijana huyu alikubali dhambi yake kama kawaida. Aliiutarifu kwa sababu ilionekana kila mtu alikuwa akisema wao pia wana dhambi, kwamba hawakuishi kwa ushindi kamili. Hilo lilimpeleka kijana huyu mahali pa uharibifu kamili.

Je, tunahubiri na kukubali Injili iliyoshindwa—injili ambayo haitoi msamaha kamili na ushindi kamili? Vijana wengi wa leo wameshangazwa. Watu wengi katika dunia ya sasa hawaelewi. Kila mtu anaweza kwenda kanisani na kujaribu kuwa mtu bora. Lakini je, kuhusu injili yenye nguvu zote, inayobadilisha maisha ya Yesu Kristo?

Mwafaka Paulo alisema kwamba Yesu anarejea kwa “. . .kanisa la utukufu, lisilo na doa, wala ubanikaji, wala aina yoyote ya kasoro; ila liwe takatifu bila doa” (Efe. 5:27). Na Yesu mwenyewe alisema “. . .Kwa kuwa wewe ni Petro, na juu ya mwamba huu nitajenga kanisa langu; na milango ya kuzimu haitashinda dhidi yake” (Math. 16:18).

Kabla sijageuzwa, nilikuwa bila shaka mtumwa wa dhambi, lakini nilitaka ushindi. Nilikuwa na uraibu wa madawa ya kulevya na pombe, lakini sikuipenda. Nilitaka kuwa huru. Nilikwenda kwa ushauri na vituo vya kurekebisha tabia kote Amerika, lakini haikufanya kazi. Sikuwa na nguvu. Ningeacha kwa siku chache au hata wiki, kisha hasira na msongo wa mawazo ulinuka, na ningerudi kwa vitu hivyo. Siku moja, nilikutana uso kwa uso na Muumba. Mkono wa Mungu Mwenye Nguvu alinigusa na kunifungua macho. Nilinyamaza dhambi zangu na nilipewa karatasi safi na moyo safi. Sikurudi nyuma kamwe. Dawa za kulevya, pombe, na pakiti mbili za sigara kwa siku zilikwisha—milele.

Sikuwa na imani kabisa na yale Mungu alikuwa anafanya. Nguvu za Mungu zilikuwa halisi. Sisingeweza kushinda peke yangu, kama hakuna mmoja wetu anavyoweza, lakini Mungu ametuhakikishia uhuru kutoka kwa ufalme wa dhambi na maisha mapya ya kuishi kwa ushindi ikiwa tutamwajibisha uhai wetu. Uwezo huu wa kushinda nguvu za dhambi na kisha kutembea kwa ushindi ndilo dunia inatafuta. Je, tunaamini kwamba Mungu anaweza kutukomboa si tu kutoka kwa uraibu wa vitu bali pia kutoka kwa hasira, ubinafsi, chuki, tamaa, na kiburi? Neno la Mungu linasema “Ikiwa tunatenda dhambi zetu, yeye ni mwaminifu na mwenye haki atatusamehe dhambi zetu, na atatusafisha na kila dhambi” (1 Yohana 1:9). Hakuna anayevutiwa na Injili iliyoshindwa, isipokuwa wale wanaoishi kwa kushangazwa kwa sababu wamechagua vitu vya dunia kuliko Mungu na Neno Lake.

Je, tuko tayari kushuhudia juu ya nguvu za ufufuo? Tunahitaji kutangaza injili ambayo inawatafuta watu kabisa kutoka kwa utumwa wa dhambi—milele. Lazima tuwe jasiri na wenye kujiamini katika imani yetu ili tuweze kuongoza watu kwa Mwalimu.

Nilikuwa nikimshuhudia mtu wakati alisema kwa sauti ya juu, “Mungu si wa kweli!” Mwana wangu wa miaka sita alifunga mdomo kwa mshangao, akapumua kwa mshangao, “Baba, amenidai uwongo!”

Mwana wangu hahitaji kushawishiwa kwamba Mungu yupo; anaamini moyo wake mzima. Dunia iliyo nje inahitaji kushawishiwa. Wanahitaji kuona kitu ambacho sayansi haiwezi kufafanua. Wanahitaji kuona kitu kinachopingana na kila matarajio.

Kitu hicho ni moyo uliobadilika kweli. Mpigaji sasa anawapenda maadui wake. Mtu mwenye tatizo la hasira sasa anawapenda wengine bila masharti. Familia zilizoharibika zinaponywa. Wawaovu waliohuruwa wanacheswa na wanaishi maisha yaliyobadilika. Tumaini, amani, upendo, na nguvu vinatolewa bure kwa wanaume na wanawake ambao wanadhani hawana matumaini. “Macho wazee wanaona, wanalemavu wanatembea, walefuo wasafishwa, viziwi wanasikia, wafu wanafufuliwa, na maskini wanatawaliwa injili” (Math. 11:5).

Je, unaishi maisha yako ili dunia ionee kazi ya Mungu ikiwa ni ya vitendo, yenye ufanisi, na halisi kila siku? Hapa kuna mambo machache ambayo Kanisa linahitaji katika wakati wetu ili tena kuwavutia waliopotea.

Utayari wa kutokea mateso

Historia itaonyesha kwamba kanisa, katika enzi zote, limepata mateso kwa ajili ya Kristo. Ilikuwa sehemu ya gharama ya kumfuata Kristo. Biblia inasema, “Bali wote watakaotaka kuishi kwa unyenyekevu ndani ya Kristo Yesu watapata mateso” (2 Tim. 3:12). Ilikuwa jambo lililotokea tu.

Leo, watu wengi wanataka ndoto ya Marekani. Watu wanaishi maisha ya maadili mazuri, ni raia wazuri, wanapata maisha mazuri, na wanaenda kanisani Jumapili. Lakini je, hilo ndilo tulioletwa kutenda? Injili ilienea kama moto wakati kanisa lilipateswa mateso na kufanya hivyo kwa hiari na kwa furaha. Ilikuwa jambo ambalo dunia haijawahi kuona—imani watu waliionyesha kwa maisha yao, na kifo chao kilikuwa kitu cha kumtumikia kwake kuwafa kwa ajili yake. Tusifurahi kutapata mateso kwa ajili ya Kristo leo.

Kukanusha nafsi (kwenye kujinyenyekeza)

Kisha Yesu akawaambia wanafunzi wake, “Ikiwa mtu anataka kuniifuata, amkanuse nafsi yake, achukue msalaba wake, na anifuate” (Math. 16:24).

Je, umewahi kuwa na shaka kwa nini Yesu anatuagiza kujikana? Baada ya yote, Alitupa tamaa na hamu, kwa hivyo kwanini lazima tujinyike? Nimesikia watu wanasema kwamba tunahitaji kulinganisha mapenzi yetu na mapenzi ya Mungu, lakini siwezi kuona hili katika Biblia. Badala yake, tunapaswa tu kukanusha mapenzi yetu na kukubali mapenzi ya Mungu.

Ninakumbuka siku ya kwanza ya mafunzo niliyojiunga nayo katika Jeshi la Wanamaji baada ya kumaliza sekondari. Karibu wanaume mia walikuwepo. Sote tulikuwa na tamaa na mawazo yetu. Tulikuwa na utambulisho wetu. Ilikuwa ya kushangaza kuona utofauti wote. Ingekuwa janga kama Marekani ingetutuma kupigana siku hiyo ya kwanza. Hivyo, walikuwa na mpango wa kutatua tatizo hili. Kwa miezi mitatu iliyofuata, walitutengeneza tena. Kimwili na kisaikolojia, tulijifunza jinsi ya kukanusha nafsi zetu na kukubali amri za wakuu wetu na mmoja kwa mwingine. Dunia mara nyingi huvutiwa na nidhamu kubwa na umoja ambao Wanamaji wanajulikana nao.

Tunapokuwa sehemu ya ufalme wa Mungu, hatuwezi kuwa na ufanisi ikiwa kila mmoja wetu atafanya anachotaka. Kikundi cha waamini kinaweza kuwa na nia njema, lakini ikiwa mtu mmoja hajakanusha nafsi yake, hatoweza kamwe kujiweka chini kwa ajili ya sababu kuu. Kuna vita inayopiganwa, na hatuwezi kuipigana peke yetu. Lazima tukatae nafsi zetu, tuungane na ndugu zetu, na tupiganie ushindi katika nyumbani mwetu, makanisa yetu, na maisha yetu.

Utii

Biblia inatutaka tuwe wa kujiweka chini:

  • kwa Mungu (Yak. 4:7).
  • [kwa wale] wanaokuwa na [roho] utawala juu yenu [sisi] (Wal. 13:17).
  • kwa kila mwamvuli wa mwanadamu kwa ajili ya Bwana (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • mmoja kwa mwenzie kwa hofu ya Mungu (Efe. 5:21).

Mara tu tunapokanusha nafsi zetu, wakati huo tu tunaweza kujiweka chini kwa wengine. Watu wengi leo wanapata ugumu mkubwa kujiweka chini kwa ndugu zao. Wengine wanahisi kuwa wako huru katika Kristo; kwa hiyo, wanaweza kufanya wanachotaka. Kuna sababu kwa nini tumeamriwa kujiweka chini kwa wengine. Ni rahisi kwetu kupoteza mafundisho thabiti tunapodhani tunaweza kubaini kila kitu peke zetu.

Tunapokuwa tumekanusha nafsi zetu kweli, tunagundua kuwa ni rahisi, na hata baraka kubwa, kujiweka chini kwa undugu. Kwa kweli, hiyo ni uhuru wa kweli. Unachotaka hakina umuhimu, na unaanza kuitegemea ndugu zako wa kiume na kike. Wakati kupata njia yako sio muhimu kwetu, basi tunaposikosea njia yetu, tuko sawa nayo. Tunapokuwa tayari kuwapotezea maisha kwa kila mmoja, tunakuwa nguvu ambayo dunia haiielewi. Dunia ilivutiwa na kanisa kwa karne nyingi, ikiitaka kile kilichokuwa nacho. Lakini kwa mshangao, leo, inaonekana kanisa kinavutiwa na dunia, kikitaka kile kilicho nayo.

Kuna nguvu katika kujiweka chini. Mamia ya miaka iliyopita, mtu aitwaye Alexander Mkuu alitawala karibu dunia yote iliyojuwa kwa kutumia nguvu za kijeshi na ujanja uliochanganywa na diplomasia.

Hadithi inasimulia kwamba Alexander na kikosi kidogo cha wanajeshi walikaribia mji uliokuwa na uzio mkubwa. Wakiwa nje ya uzio, Alexander alinukia sauti yake na kuhitaji kuona mfalme. Mfalme alipoingia, Alexander alisisitiza kwamba mfalme atawasilisha mji na wakaazi wake kwa Alexander na kikosi chake kidogo cha wapiganaji.

Mfalme alicheka, “Kwanini nitanikubali? Huwezi kuitukanga!” Hivyo, Alexander alitoa onyesho. Aliamuru wanajeshi wake waingie kwa mstari moja na waanze kutembea. Aliwaongoza wakatembee moja kwa moja kuelekea kwenye mwamba mwerevu.

Watu wa mji walikusanyika kwenye ukuta na kutazama kwa kimya walioshtuka huku wanajeshi wa Alexander, mmoja mmoja, wakitembea bila kusita, wakiruka juu ya mwamba hadi vifo vyao! Baada ya wanajeshi kumi kufa, Alexander aliagiza wengine warudi upande wake. Watu wa mji na mfalme walikubali mara moja kumkia Alexander Mkuu. Walitambua kwamba ikiwa wanaume wachache walikuwa tayari kujitoa uhai kwa amri ya kiongozi huyu mwenye nguvu, basi hakuna kitu kingeweza kuzuia ushindi wake wa mwisho.

Utii wa Amri

Kujiweka chini na utii huenda pamoja. Ikiwa uko tayari kujiweka chini kwa kitu au mtu, utataka kumnyang’anywa. Inakuwa muhimu kukubali wale waliotushika juu yetu, hasa Mungu Mwenyezi Mbinguni. Ikiwa tunapata taabu kujiweka chini, kawaida tutakuwa na taabu pia kwa utii. Mungu ailaze kama tukiwa tunaamini kuwa ni bora kufanya mambo peke zetu bila ndugu zetu.

Upendo

“Kwa hili wote watu watamfahamu kuwa ninyi ni wanafunzi wangu, ikiwa mnapendana kwao” (Yohana 13:35).

Watu hupiga mikono na kuwapigia watu pembezoni mwa barabara, au watafungulia mzee mlango. Watu kwa ujumla ni wapendanao hadi kitu hakikiendi kwa mpangilio wao. Kisha wanaweza kuwa ngumu sana. Je, hiyo ndiyo njia ambayo kanisa linaonyesha upendo wake kwa dunia leo? Mradi tu kila kitu kinaenda vizuri, na hakuna anayegusa haki zetu, sote tunapendana. Kisha mara tu kunapokuwa jambo la kupigana, tunavaa “mikoba ya ngumi”. Je, Biblia haisemi “upendo huvumilia yote, unaamini yote, unatumaini yote, huvumilia yote” (1 Kor. 13:7)? Upendo wa kweli unaonekana tunapokutana na matatizo au wakati ndugu anafanya jambo la kujeruhi sisi. Hilo ndilo upendo utakaomuonyesha dunia sisi ni wanafunzi wa Yesu.

Je, tunampenda ndugu yetu vya kutosha kumsaidia anapohitaji? Labda anapata kupotoka bila kujua kutoka kwa Mungu katika eneo fulani. Tunampenda kwa kiasi gani? Watu wengine hufikiri upendo ni tu kuzungumza mambo mazuri kwa kila mmoja, lakini ikiwa tunampenda ndugu kwa kweli, tutamtembelea kwa upendo na kumwambia ukweli kwa uwazi. Kisha ikiwa tunaishi kwa tabia ya kujikana nafsi na kujiweka chini kwa undugu, itaenda vizuri. Mungu ailaze tu tukasirika kwa ndugu anayetufunulia makosa yetu.

Tunapochagua kushiriki mateso pamoja na watu wa Mungu na tukanusha nafsi zetu, basi tunathamini wakati ndugu au dada anatufunulia katika maisha yetu. Hatutaruhusu nafsi zetu kuudhiwa.

Kuteseka kwa ajili ya na pamoja na kila mmoja, pamoja na kujikana nafsi kwa ajili ya kila mmoja, mara nyingi huunda upendo thabiti kwa kila mmoja. Aina hii ya upendo ndiyo ambayo dunia karibu nasi haitambui lakini inaitaka sana. Dunia inazidi kuwa yenye ubinafsi na kujitegemea kadiri siku zinavyopita. Hatuwezi kupoteza fursa zetu za kuonyesha kwao nguvu za Mungu kwa upendo wetu kwa kila mmoja.

Watu wa Mungu katika enzi zote walikuwa na nafasi yao ya kumtumikia Mfalme na kusambaza ujumbe wa Ufalme wa Mungu, lakini wametimiza kazi yao na wameenda peponi. Leo ni wakati wetu. Mashamba yameiva kwa mavuno. Tuchangamke na, kwa msaada wa Mungu, tuhifadhi kanisa la utukufu la Yesu Kristo kwa watoto wetu, kizazi kijacho.

“O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are His judgments, and his ways past finding out! For who hath known the mind of the Lord? Or who hath been his counsellor? Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again? For of Him, and through Him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen” (Rom. 11:33–36).

What an exuberant and expressive exclamation written by Apostle Paul! As we look at a new hymn and hymn writer again, let’s keep our minds alert and hearts open to see the hand of God at work.

Matthew Bridges was born at Malden, Essex, in England, on July 14, 1800. He began to publish verses in 1825 and continued until he had published two small volumes of hymns—Hymns of the Heart (1848) and The Passion of Jesus (1852). From here, I will continue with the story by giving a brief history of the church life of our hymnodist.

The hymn writer we are studying in this article was a part of the Anglican Church of England. Around the middle of the 19th century, he became dissatisfied with the church group he was with and found himself following the leading of John Henry Newman in what was called the Oxford Movement. According to hymnologist Albert Bailey, this movement centered on, “Claiming for their Anglican Church lineal descent from the original Apostolic Church.” In pursuit of this, the organization’s followers studied the ancient history of the church, its doctrine, and especially its liturgy. In doing so, they discovered a wealth of Greek and Latin hymnody from the earliest centuries of the Christian church.

As sadly, we find many factions in the Christian church today, so also was the scope of things going on in the mid–1800s. The Oxford Movement seemed in some ways to be a competition between the old and the new way of doing things. In the case of the figure in our story today, it seems he saw a more stable path forward in keeping the old traditions of the mother church, yet he also seemed to have a real, living faith in our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Now, I want to interject here that I trust his decision was made in all good conscience toward God, even though we look on today from an Anabaptist viewpoint and question his reasons for doing so.

We will continue with our story here. Matthew Bridges converted to Roman Catholicism and, wanting to share in the rich hymnic tradition of the Protestant Church, began writing original hymns. Mr. Bridges’ hymns are marked by spirituality and genuine power. One of his hymns we love and enjoy is “Rise, Glorious Conqueror.” Undoubtedly, his greatest hymn is “Crown Him with Many Crowns.” It first appeared in his book The Passion of Jesus, and was originally given the title “The Song of the Seraphs.”

There is an interesting background connected to this hymn, including how there came to be 12 verses. Understandably, only a portion of those verses are being sung today. The selection of verses depends on the hymnal.

Matthew Bridges originally penned the song in 1851. He wrote six stanzas, all based upon Rev. 19:12: “ ... and on His head were many crowns.” The edition by Bridges continued until the 1870s when a devout Anglican clergyman named Godfrey Thring came along. Godfrey was concerned that this popular hymn allowed catholic theology to be sung by protestant congregations. His concerns centered perhaps on Bridges’ original second verse, where he referenced the Blessed Virgin Mary. In light of this, Thring wrote six new stanzas and published it in his Hymns and Sacred Lyrics in 1874.

The 12 stanzas have been mixed and matched down through the years. Interestingly, of the six verses most commonly appearing in hymnals today, three were written by Bridges and three by Thring. The hymn, as published in the Hymns of the Church songbook, completely omits original verse 2 and uses verses 1, 3, 4, part of 5, and part of 6 out of Bridges’ original six verses. The stanzas we sing in that book are highlighted in the selection of verses below. Also included as well are the six couplets by Thring.

Crown Him with Many Crowns

—Bridges

Crown Him with many crowns, the Lamb upon His throne;
Hark! how the heavenly anthems drowns all music but its own;
Awake, my soul, and sing of Him who died for thee,
And hail Him as thy matchless King through all eternity.

Crown Him the Virgin’s Son! The God Incarnate born—
Whose arm those crimson trophies won which now His brow adorn!
Fruit of the mystic Rose as of that Rose the Stem:
The Root, whence mercy ever flows—the Babe of Bethlehem!

Crown Him the Lord of peace! Whose power a scepter sways,
From pole to pole, that wars may cease, absorbed in prayer and praise:
His reign shall know no end, and round His pierced feet
Fair flowers of paradise extend their fragrance ever sweet.

Crown Him the Lord of love! Behold His hands and side—
Rich wounds, yet visible above, in beauty glorified:
No angel in the sky can fully bear that sight,
But downward bends his burning eye at mysteries so bright!

Crown Him the Lord of years! The Potentate of time—
Creator of the rolling spheres, ineffably sublime!
Glassed in a sea of light, where everlasting waves
Reflect His throne—the Infinite! Who lives—and loves—and saves.

Crown Him the Lord of heaven! One with the Father known,
And the blest Spirit, through Him given from yonder triune throne!
All hail! Redeemer—Hail! For Thou hast died for me;
Thy praise shall never, never fail throughout eternity!

Crown Him with Many Crowns

—Thring

Crown Him with crowns of gold, all nations great and small,
Crown Him, ye martyred saints of old, the Lamb once slain for all;
The Lamb once slain for them who bring their praises now,
As jewels for the diadem that girds His sacred brow.

Crown Him the Son of God before the worlds began,
And ye, who tread where He hath trod, crown Him the Son of man;
Who every grief hath known that wrings the human breast,
And takes and bears them for His own, that all in Him may rest.

Crown Him the Lord of light, Who o’er a darkened world
In robes of glory infinite His fiery flag unfurled.
And bore it raised on high, in heaven—in earth—beneath,
To all the sign of victory o’er Satan, sin, and death.

Crown Him the Lord of life Who triumphed o’er the grave,
And rose victorious in the strife for those He came to save;
His glories now we sing Who died, and rose on high.
Who died, eternal life to bring and lives that death may die.

Crown Him of lords the Lord, Who over all doth reign
Who once on earth, the incarnate Word, for ransomed sinners slain,
Now lives in realms of light, where saints with angels sing
Their songs before Him day and night, their God, Redeemer, King.

Crown Him the Lord of heaven, enthroned in worlds above;
Crown Him the King, to whom is given the wondrous name of Love,
Crown Him with many crowns, as thrones before Him fall.
Crown Him, ye kings, with many crowns, for He is King of all.

Matthew Bridges lived his latter years in the province of Quebec, Canada, then returned to England before his passing from earth on October 6, 1894, at the ripe old age of 94. Although we don’t find many details about his life, he has left one of the greatest hymns in our hands today.

A great part of this song’s enduring quality is the tune it is paired with. This refrain was written especially for this song by Sir George Job Elvey in 1868 and was given the name of Diademata. In Greek, the word diademata means “a royal crown”—a fitting name for this stirring melody. Hymnology scholar J. R. Watson agrees with this when he observes, “Diademata makes a magnificent setting for the text, march-like and joyful without ever becoming mechanical or strident.”

May our congregations continue our practice of corporate, whole-hearted singing, lifting our voices in praise to the Lord in the assembly of the saints! Crown Him, our Lord Jesus Christ, with many crowns, for he is worthy!

„O welch eine Tiefe des Reichtums sowohl der Weisheit als auch der Erkenntnis Gottes! wie unerforschlich sind seine Gerichte, und unergründlich seine Wege! Denn wer hat den Sinn des Herrn erkannt? Oder wer ist sein Ratgeber gewesen? Oder wer hat ihm zuvor etwas gegeben, dass es ihm wieder vergolten werde? Denn von ihm und durch ihn und zu ihm sind alle Dinge; ihm sei die Herrlichkeit in Ewigkeit. Amen“ (Röm. 11:33–36).

Was für ein übersprudelnder und expressiver Ausruf, geschrieben vom Apostel Paulus! Wenn wir uns erneut einem neuen Lied und einem Liederdichter zuwenden, so wollen wir unsere Gedanken wach und unsere Herzen offen halten, um die Hand Gottes am Werk zu sehen.

Matthew Bridges wurde am 14. Juli 1800 in Malden, Essex, in England, geboren. Er begann 1825, Verse zu veröffentlichen, und setzte dies fort, bis er zwei kleine Bände mit Hymnen herausgegeben hatte—Hymns of the Heart (1848) und The Passion of Jesus (1852). Von hier aus fahre ich mit der Geschichte fort, indem ich eine kurze Darstellung des kirchlichen Lebens unseres Liederdichters gebe.

Der Liederdichter, den wir in diesem Artikel untersuchen, gehörte der anglikanischen Church of England an. Um die Mitte des 19. Jahrhunderts wurde er mit der Kirche, der er angehörte, unzufrieden und fand sich letztlich dabei, der Führung John Henry Newmans in der sogenannten Oxford-Bewegung zu folgen. Nach dem Hymnologen Albert Bailey konzentrierte sich diese Bewegung darauf, „für ihre anglikanische Kirche eine direkte Abstammung von der ursprünglichen apostolischen Kirche in Anspruch zu nehmen.“ In diesem Bestreben studierten die Anhänger die alte Kirchengeschichte, deren Lehre und besonders deren Liturgie. Dabei entdeckten sie einen reichen Bestand an griechischer und lateinischer Hymnodie aus den frühesten Jahrhunderten der christlichen Kirche.

So wie wir heute leider viele Fraktionen in der christlichen Kirche finden, so war auch das Spannungsfeld Mitte des 1800. Jahrhunderts vielfältig. Die Oxford-Bewegung schien in mancher Hinsicht ein Wettstreit zwischen altem und neuem Vorgehen zu sein. Im Fall der Gestalt unserer heutigen Geschichte scheint er einen beständigeren Weg im Festhalten an den alten Traditionen der Mutterkirche gesehen zu haben; zugleich schien er aber auch einen echten, lebendigen Glauben an unseren Herrn und Erlöser Jesus Christus zu haben. Hier möchte ich einfügen, dass ich darauf vertraue, seine Entscheidung sei in allem guten Gewissens vor Gott getroffen worden, auch wenn wir heute aus anabaptistischer Sicht seine Beweggründe hinterfragen.

Wir fahren mit unserer Geschichte fort. Matthew Bridges konvertierte zum römischen Katholizismus und begann, um an der reichen hymnischen Tradition der protestantischen Kirche teilzuhaben, eigene Hymnen zu schreiben. Mr. Bridges’ Hymnen zeichnen sich durch Spiritualität und echte Kraft aus. Eine seiner Hymnen, die wir lieben und genießen, ist „Rise, Glorious Conqueror.“ Zweifellos aber ist seine größte Hymne „Crown Him with Many Crowns.“ Sie erschien erstmals in seinem Buch The Passion of Jesus und trug ursprünglich den Titel „The Song of the Seraphs.“

Zu dieser Hymne gehört ein interessanter Hintergrund, einschließlich der Frage, wie es zu 12 Strophen kam. Verständlicherweise wird heute nur ein Teil dieser Strophen gesungen. Die Auswahl der Strophen hängt vom Gesangbuch ab.

Matthew Bridges verfasste das Lied ursprünglich 1851. Er schrieb sechs Strophen, alle basierend auf Offb. 19:12: „... und auf seinem Haupt waren viele Kronen.“ Die Ausgabe von Bridges bestand bis in die 1870er Jahre, als ein frommer anglikanischer Geistlicher namens Godfrey Thring auftauchte. Godfrey befürchtete, dass diese populäre Hymne katholische Theologie in protestantischen Gemeinden salonfähig machte. Seine Bedenken richteten sich möglicherweise gegen Bridges’ ursprüngliche zweite Strophe, in der er die selige Jungfrau Maria erwähnte. Vor diesem Hintergrund schrieb Thring sechs neue Strophen und veröffentlichte sie 1874 in seinem Hymns and Sacred Lyrics.

Die 12 Strophen wurden im Laufe der Jahre gemischt und in unterschiedlicher Zusammenstellung verwendet. Interessanterweise stammen von den sechs Strophen, die heute am häufigsten in Gesangbüchern erscheinen, drei von Bridges und drei von Thring. Die in Hymns of the Church veröffentlichte Fassung lässt die ursprüngliche Strophe 2 vollständig weg und verwendet aus Bridges’ ursprünglichen sechs Strophen die Strophen 1, 3, 4, einen Teil von 5 und einen Teil von 6. Die Strophen, die wir in diesem Buch singen, sind in der folgenden Auswahl hervorgehoben. Ebenfalls enthalten sind die sechs Couplets von Thring.

Kröne Ihn mit vielen Kronen

—Bridges

Kröne Ihn mit vielen Kronen, das Lamm auf seinem Thron;
Hört! wie die himmlischen Anthemen jede Musik verschlingen, außer ihrer eigenen;
Erwache, meine Seele, und sing von Ihm, der für dich starb,
Und grüße Ihn als deinen unvergleichlichen König durch alle Ewigkeit.

Kröne Ihn, den Sohn der Jungfrau! Den fleischgewordenen Gott geboren—
Dessen Arm jene purpurnen Trophäen gewann, die nun sein Haupt schmücken!
Frucht der mystischen Rose, wie des Rosenstammes Teil:
Die Wurzel, aus der Barmherzigkeit stets fließt—das Kindlein von Bethlehem!

Kröne Ihn, den Herrn des Friedens! Dessen Macht ein Zepter schwingt,
Von Pol zu Pol, dass Kriege enden, versunken in Gebet und Lobpreis:
Sein Reich wird kein Ende kennen, und rund um seine durchbohrten Füße
Breiten sich die schönen Blumen des Paradieses aus und verströmen ihren immer süßen Duft.

Kröne Ihn, den Herrn der Liebe! Schau seine Hände und die Seite—
Reiche Wunden, doch oben sichtbar, in Schönheit verherrlicht:
Kein Engel am Himmel kann dieses Bild voll ertragen,
Sondern neigt sein brennendes Auge hernieder bei Geheimnissen so hell!

Kröne Ihn, den Herrn der Jahre! Den Herrscher über die Zeit—
Schöpfer der rollenden Sphären, unbeschreiblich erhaben!
Eingebettet in ein Meer des Lichts, wo ewige Wellen
Sein Thronbild spiegeln—den Unendlichen! Der lebt—und liebt—und rettet.

Kröne Ihn, den Herrn des Himmels! Eins mit dem Vater bekannt,
Und dem seligen Geist, der durch Ihn gegeben ist vom dreieinigen Thron dort oben!
Heil dir! Erlöser—Heil! Denn Du bist für mich gestorben;
Dein Lob wird niemals, niemals versagen durch die Ewigkeit!

Kröne Ihn mit vielen Kronen

—Thring

Kröne Ihn mit goldenen Kronen, alle Völker groß und klein,
Kröne Ihn, ihr gemarterten Heiligen von einst, das Lamm, das einst für alle geschlachtet ward;
Das Lamm, einst für jene geschlachtet, die nun ihre Loblieder bringen,
Als Juwelen für das Diadem, das seine heilige Stirn umfängt.

Kröne Ihn, den Sohn Gottes, bevor die Welt begann,
Und ihr, die ihr wandelt, wo Er gewandelt ist, krönt Ihn, den Sohn des Menschen;
Der jedes Leid gekannt hat, das die menschliche Brust quält,
Und nimmt und trägt sie für sein Eigen, damit alle in Ihm Ruhe finden mögen.

Kröne Ihn, den Herrn des Lichts, der über eine verdunkelte Welt
In Gewändern unendlicher Herrlichkeit sein feuriges Banner entfaltete.
Und trug es hoch erhoben, im Himmel—in der Erde—darunter,
Als Zeichen des Sieges über Satan, Sünde und Tod für alle.

Kröne Ihn, den Herrn des Lebens, der über das Grab triumphierte,
Und siegreich auferstand im Kampf für jene, die Er retten kam;
Seine Herrlichkeiten singen wir jetzt, der starb und hoch auferstand.
Der starb, um ewiges Leben zu bringen, und lebt, damit der Tod sterben möge.

Kröne Ihn, der Herren Herr, der über allen herrscht,
Der einst auf Erden, das fleischgewordene Wort, für freigekaufte Sünder hingeschlachtet wurde,
Nun lebt in Reichen des Lichts, wo Heilige mit Engeln singen
Ihre Lieder vor Ihm Tag und Nacht, ihrem Gott, Erlöser, König.

Kröne Ihn, den Herrn des Himmels, erhoben in Welten oben;
Kröne Ihn, den König, dem der wundersame Name der Liebe gegeben ist,
Kröne Ihn mit vielen Kronen, wie Throne vor Ihm fallen.
Kröne Ihn, ihr Könige, mit vielen Kronen, denn Er ist König über alle.

Matthew Bridges verbrachte seine letzten Jahre in der Provinz Québec, Kanada, kehrte dann vor seinem Tod wieder nach England zurück und verschied am 6. Oktober 1894 im hohen Alter von 94 Jahren. Zwar finden sich nicht viele Details über sein Leben, doch hat er uns eine der größten Hymnen hinterlassen.

Ein großer Teil der bleibenden Qualität dieses Liedes liegt in der Melodie, mit der es verbunden ist. Dieser Refrain wurde speziell für dieses Lied 1868 von Sir George Job Elvey geschrieben und erhielt den Namen Diademata. Auf Griechisch bedeutet das Wort diademata „eine königliche Krone“—ein passender Name für diese ergreifende Melodie. Der Hymnologie-Gelehrte J. R. Watson stimmt dem zu, wenn er beobachtet: „Diademata bildet eine großartige Fassung für den Text, marschartig und freudig, ohne je mechanisch oder schrill zu werden.“

Mögen unsere Gemeinden die Übung des gemeinsamen, von Herzen kommenden Singens fortsetzen und unsere Stimmen im Lobpreis dem Herrn in der Versammlung der Heiligen erheben! Krönt Ihn, unseren Herrn Jesus Christus, mit vielen Kronen, denn er ist würdig!

Bezugsquellen: A Treasury of Hymn Stories, hymnary.org, umc-discipleship.org, FBC

“So, what brings you in today?” I asked Ben, a 40-year-old man who was sitting across from me.

“Well,” he answered. “I have a few different symptoms. The biggest one is that I am always tired, but I’ve also been gaining weight, and my knees hurt some in the mornings.”

I mentally began to go through what doctors call a differential diagnosis – things that can cause the cluster of symptoms that a patient has. I usually let the patient explain what symptoms he is experiencing and then ask questions to try to hone in on the specific diagnosis.

Ben went on for a little while longer. Then, he proceeded to pull out a piece of paper. “So, Doctor,” he told me. “I’ve done some research into my diagnosis, and I think these are tests that I need to have done to work things up.”

I looked at the list. It was pretty long and included some things I probably would have ordered anyway, like a blood count and thyroid level, but also some very odd things like a Vitamin B1 level and a DHEA level. He also wanted a CT Scan of his head, chest, and abdomen.

“This is a lot of testing,” I said. “I’m not sure we need to do all of it. Can we talk a little bit more about your symptoms and then try to hone in on what testing would be best to sort it out?”

Ben was not impressed. “I have done my research!” He told me firmly. “These days, with the internet, you can find out things that your doctor wouldn’t tell you about – maybe things he doesn’t even know to test for. The problem is that I need YOU to order these things for me so my insurance will cover them. Otherwise, I wouldn’t even be here.”

With that, we’ll leave Ben and his uncomfortable doctor behind. There have always been patients who brought in articles from magazines telling the reader, “Six things your doctor won’t tell you about your health” and listing testing that should be done. It does seem to have gotten worse.

A lot of patients know more than their doctors. They can search for their symptoms on the web and find out all sorts of things that could cause those symptoms.

Beyond that, artificial intelligence is smart. Chat GPT, an artificial intelligence platform, was able to pass the three parts of the US Medical Licensure Exam.1 It didn’t do terribly well— it only got just above a passing grade, but I suppose that’s good enough that it could open an office across the street from mine and start seeing patients.

In some ways letting patients have access to this level of information is a good thing. Doctors aren’t some sort of high priests who are given special rights to access the Holiest of Holies of medical information. More than that, doctors are anything but perfect, and you have only to read online reviews to see that they don’t listen well, botch procedures, and struggle with difficult diagnoses.

It can be challenging, though, when patients believe that they know more than their doctor. I have always said that if you know more than your doctor, either you need a healthy dose of humility or a new doctor— or maybe both.

Get Wisdom!

Proverbs 4:5-9 says, “Get wisdom, get understanding: forget it not; neither decline from the words of my mouth. Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee. Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding. Exalt her, and she shall promote thee: she shall bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her. She shall give to thine head an ornament of grace: a crown of glory shall she deliver to thee.”

Proverbs 18:15 speaks of getting knowledge, but it indicates that before we seek knowledge, we should make certain that we have wisdom and understanding.

The author of the book of Proverbs was Solomon. We know that early in his reign he had a dream in which God appeared to him and offered him whatever he desired. In his humility, Solomon asked for an understanding heart, so that he would be able to wisely lead such a great people (I Kings 3:9,10).

When we look at knowledge, it is simply a group of facts— blocks of information that need to be assembled into some sort of coherent pattern. Wisdom and understanding are the tools with which we make sense of the knowledge that we have acquired.

Wisdom lets us judge the accuracy of the sources of “knowledge” as well. It helps us to ask the question, “Is this person trying to sell me something? Do they actually have any scientific studies that indicate that what they say is true?”

These are two questions that I ask when I look at a website. Are there links to products that are being sold to me, and is the advertising clearly separated from the articles? More than that, are there links to studies that support what is being claimed? If there are, how big were those studies? If a study has only 12 people in it, it is not large enough to give accurate information.

Robert Harris made an acronym CARS, that helps sort out whether information on a website is valid. Credibility, past Accuracy, Reasonableness, and Supporting information are all important to look at to see if we should value the information on a website.2

Unfortunately, many people who claim to have the answers to living long and healthy lives are actually trying to sell books, supplements, and a variety of other products. One prominent doctor who promotes better health through the use of supplements (that he sells) has managed to accrue enough money through the process that he stated in a 2017 affidavit that he was worth in excess of 100 million dollars. This doesn’t mean that he has nothing to offer, but it does say that he has some bias towards recommending things he is selling.

The American Medical Association has guidelines for doctors to sell products out of their offices ethically. Those guidelines say that the products should serve a particular urgent need (say, crutches at an Orthopedic office), have scientific validity for their use, and that doctors should offer information about other ways that patients can get the same products elsewhere.3 More than that, doctors should reveal to their patients any financial interest that they have in the product that is being offered to the patient.

Confirmation Bias

Most of us read in order to confirm the things we already believe. I see this when people read the Bible— somehow, people can read the Bible and completely ignore Scriptures that contradict their behaviors in terms of political involvement or modesty of dress but believe that they are following all things of the Scripture.

In the same way, each one of us can find stories and information that reinforce our beliefs about doctors and medicine. If we believe that doctors are simply after money and are unethical and prescribe medicines that are toxic to patients, we can find articles that confirm that. On the other hand, if we look for stories that tear down alternative medicine theories, we can find those articles too.

The important thing is that we approach the question looking for real answers and understanding that science doesn’t know everything.

As an example, we do not have good treatments for people who have Long COVID symptoms. That doesn’t mean that many people who suffered through COVID months later aren’t suffering from things like mental fog and fatigue, but it does mean that there is not a single medication that has done better than sugar pills in studies to get rid of those symptoms.

In the absence of scientifically proven treatment plans, many clinics have developed their own treatment courses, using a mixture of supplements and even hyperbaric oxygen treatments. Are these helpful? I don’t know, but I do know that those marketing them will confidently claim that they have an extremely high success rate in curing people if they are simply willing to follow (and pay for) the treatment plan.

More than that, when people are researching their symptoms, they tend to choose what diagnoses they think are likely based on their underlying personality types. Some people are prone to catastrophize— that is, they immediately believe the worst possible outcome of any given scenario they are presented with. These people will type in their symptoms and will come to the conclusion that they have cancer with only days or weeks to live. As God told Hezekiah, it is time for them to set their house in order.

On the other hand, there are plenty of people who have optimistic personalities. They type in their symptom list and come to the conclusion that they have a mild viral illness and will feel better in a few days.

The whole point of having a medical provider review things is that the practitioner can (hopefully) sort out the likely things from the unlikely ones. They don’t deal with the emotional overlay that patients do, so they can objectively decide how many tests to order and what type of tests to order in order to come up with a diagnosis.

Doctors Can Identify Dangerous Situations

I remember seeing a patient years ago who came in to see me with what she thought was a sinus infection. She was in her 20s and said that she had a pounding sensation in her head and a lot of pressure.

She didn’t really have any drainage or fever and none of the typical symptoms of a sinus infection, but sinusitis seemed like the most likely diagnosis that she could come up with.

I took one look at her and didn’t like what I saw. For one thing, she was extremely pale. For another, her pulse rate was quite fast – 130 beats a minute at rest. When I examined her, I found nothing that indicated that she had a sinus infection.

“Jenny,” I told her. “I need you to go to the hospital and get a stat blood count. I’m afraid you are really anemic— although I don’t know why. Wait at the lab and I will talk to you once I get the results back.”

It was perhaps 20 minutes later that I got an urgent call from the hospital laboratory. “Dr. Waldron,” the voice on the other end said. “We have a critical lab result for you…”

Jenny’s hemoglobin was 4.6 (normal is between 12 and 16), and she ended up getting a transfusion. What she didn’t get was treatment for a sinus infection.

Chest pain is a classic symptom that can point to an underlying heart condition. At the same time, it could simply indicate esophageal reflux (acid in the esophagus) or inflammation in a rib or muscle. I probably see a couple of patients every day who have this symptom.

The majority of them need a simple treatment, but a few of them need to be sent urgently to the hospital for a complete heart evaluation. I don’t know how an online search engine will know which direction to indicate for a person to seek after reviewing their symptoms.

At best, an online resource will refer a user to seek emergency services or their local doctor.

Not All Doctors Are Equal

Roughly 50 percent of doctors finished in the bottom half of their Medical School class. Just because someone didn’t have top marks in Medical School doesn’t mean that they don’t have adequate knowledge to treat an ailment. Perhaps the most important knowledge that a doctor needs is to know when he doesn’t know.

It is still challenging for patients to know whether they are dealing with someone who will help them. When you meet a doctor, you tend to judge them based on their “bedside manner.” Most of us look for someone who exudes confidence and seems to know what they are doing.

Confidence does not equal competence, and there are many doctors (and people in other fields) who have high levels of confidence in themselves but are not really competent to take care of the situation at hand.

Here is where doing some research can help. First, your doctor has online reviews, and those reviews will indicate something about the level of care they provide for patients. Second, if what your healthcare provider tells you seems really odd, it is easy to do a little research on the condition that you are supposedly dealing with and see if the symptoms line up and if the treatment seems reasonable.

It is important to realize that humans are not like vehicles. What I mean by that is that there is no scan tool that healthcare providers can hook up and generate all of the error codes and then fix the things that generate those codes.

Even if healthcare providers are certain of the diagnosis, some patients do not respond to the first or even the second treatment that is available. That doesn’t mean that the diagnosis or the treatment was wrong, but that people are not clones of each other and some respond better to one type of treatment than another.

Maybe someday we will have some type of genetic testing that tells us right off what the perfect medication or treatment plan is for a given illness, but that day seems a long way off.

A final thing to mention is that good doctors will not feel threatened by their patients asking questions or doing research. There are times when a patient will ask me about a new treatment that I am not familiar with, and I need to do my own research.

Those scenarios are not upsetting for me but rather a learning opportunity. “I’m not familiar with that,” I will tell my patient. “Let me do a little research and talk to some specialists that I trust, and I will call you later this week and let you know what I find out.”

Sometimes I investigate and find that the treatment is expensive and seems to provide mixed or little benefit, but sometimes it is an improvement over the past ways of doing things. Doctors need to learn and adjust their style of practicing medicine as we learn new things about diseases and how the human body responds to them.

Humility is Needed

The longer I practice medicine, the less I feel that I know. It isn’t that I have developed dementia, but rather that I realize that there are numerous diseases that we don’t have good treatments for. The human body is amazingly complex. There are 36 trillion cells in the human body, and normally, they all work together perfectly; the problem is figuring out what to do when they don’t.

The Dunning-Kruger Effect is something that affects many fields in which people with limited knowledge and skill significantly overestimate their abilities in that field. Studies have shown that 65 percent of Americans believe that they have above-average IQs.4 Statistically, this isn’t possible. Fifty percent of any group of people will have above-average IQs, and the other 50 percent will be below-average. That’s how the IQ scale is set up.

While this effect is present for doctors, it is also present for patients. “Doing your research” is not the same thing as spending four years in Medical School, another three years in a residency training program, and continuing to stay abreast of developments in medicine through a variety of educational courses. We all would do well to listen better and realize our limitations.

The fact that your mother’s cousin took milkweed extract and felt much better from similar symptoms to yours is interesting. Whether the milkweed extract helped them get over their illness, whether there was a placebo effect, or they were just going to get better anyway, regardless of what they took, is up for debate.

True Wisdom

I have mentioned wisdom already, and I would finish with that. True wisdom is realizing that healing comes from God. Psalms 103:3 says of God, “Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases.”

Healing doesn’t come from antibiotics or chemotherapy. It doesn’t come from taking the right supplements or even eating a healthy diet. Healing comes because God touches us, right down to the tiniest parts of our cells and immune system, and makes things whole again.

I do believe that sometimes He works through medicine, but other times He works through the effective, fervent prayer of righteous men and women. (James 5:16)

With all of our knowledge, it is easy for us to get puffed up with pride and believe that we need no one else. We live in a world that is teeming with knowledge and a world in which wisdom has taken a back seat.

We must choose the source of our information carefully and realize that we don’t know everything. Maybe the reason why the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom is because it is the first step to us laying aside our pride and realizing that we are a tiny part of Creation. Only then, can we humbly listen and learn and receive healing.

“Så, hva bringer deg hit i dag?” spurte jeg Ben, en 40 år gammel mann som satt overfor meg.

“Vel,” svarte han. “Jeg har noen forskjellige symptomer. Det største er at jeg alltid er trøtt, men jeg har også gått opp i vekt, og knærne mine gjør litt vondt om morgenen.”

Jeg begynte mentalt å gå gjennom det legene kaller en differensialdiagnose – ting som kan forårsake den symptomklyngen en pasient har. Jeg lar vanligvis pasienten forklare hvilke symptomer han opplever, og så stiller jeg spørsmål for å prøve å spisse inn den konkrete diagnosen.

Ben fortsatte litt lengre. Så dro han fram et ark. “Så, doktor,” sa han til meg. “Jeg har gjort litt research på diagnosen min, og jeg tror disse er tester jeg trenger å få gjort for å finne ut av ting.”

Jeg så på listen. Den var ganske lang og inkluderte noen ting jeg sannsynligvis uansett ville ha bestilt, som en blodtelling og skjoldbruskkjertelnivå, men også noen merkelige ting som et nivå av vitamin B1 og et DHEA-nivå. Han ønsket også CT-skanning av hode, brystkasse og mage.

“Dette er mye testing,” sa jeg. “Jeg er ikke sikker på at vi trenger å gjøre alt dette. Kan vi snakke litt mer om symptomene dine og så prøve å spisse inn hvilke tester som vil være best for å avklare det?”

Ben var ikke imponert. “Jeg har gjort min research!” sa han bestemt. “I disse dager, med internett, kan du finne ut ting legen din ikke ville fortalt deg – kanskje ting han ikke engang vet å teste for. Problemet er at jeg trenger DEG til å bestille disse tingene for meg slik at forsikringen min dekker dem. Ellers ville jeg ikke engang vært her.”

Med det lar vi Ben og hans ukomfortable lege ligge igjen. Det har alltid vært pasienter som har tatt med artikler fra magasiner og fortalt leseren: “Seks ting legen din ikke vil fortelle deg om helsen din” og listet tester som burde gjøres. Det ser ut til å ha blitt verre.

Mange pasienter vet mer enn legene sine. De kan søke på symptomene sine på nettet og finne ut alle slags ting som kan forårsake disse symptomene.

I tillegg er kunstig intelligens smart. Chat GPT, en plattform for kunstig intelligens, klarte å bestå de tre delene av den amerikanske legeautorisasjonseksamenen (USMLE).1 Den gjorde det ikke veldig bra— den fikk bare så vidt over karaktergrensen, men jeg antar at det er godt nok til at den kunne åpne en praksis tvers over gaten for meg og begynne å se pasienter.

På noen måter er det en god ting at pasienter får tilgang til dette kunnskapsnivået. Leger er ikke noen slags yppersteprester som har spesielle rettigheter til å få tilgang til det helligste av det hellige innen medisinsk informasjon. Mer enn det, leger er alt annet enn perfekte, og det er bare å lese anmeldelser på nettet for å se at de ikke lytter godt, bommer på prosedyrer og strever med vanskelige diagnoser.

Det kan likevel være utfordrende når pasienter tror de vet mer enn legen sin. Jeg har alltid sagt at om du vet mer enn legen din, trenger du enten en solid dose ydmykhet eller en ny lege— eller kanskje begge deler.

Få visdom!

Ordspråkene 4:5-9 sier: “Få visdom, få forstand! Glem det ikke, ei svik fra min munns ord. Forlat henne ikke, så bærer hun deg frem; hold henne kjær, så vokter hun deg. Visdom er det fremste; skaff deg visdom! Ja, for alt du skaffer deg, skaff deg forstand. Forherlig henne, så gir hun deg ære; hun fører deg til verdighet når du holder henne om.”

Ordspråkene 18:15 taler om å få kunnskap, men indikerer at før vi søker kunnskap, bør vi sikre oss at vi har visdom og forstand.

Forfatteren av Ordspråkene var Salomo. Vi vet at tidlig i hans regjeringstid hadde han en drøm der Gud viste seg for ham og tilbød ham hva han måtte ønske. I sin ydmykhet ba Salomo om et forstandig hjerte, så han kunne lede et så stort folk med visdom (1. Kongebok 3:9,10).

Når vi ser på kunnskap, er det simpelthen en samling fakta— informasjonsblokker som må settes sammen til et slags sammenhengende mønster. Visdom og forstand er verktøyene vi bruker for å gi mening til kunnskapen vi har tilegnet oss.

Visdom lar oss også bedømme nøyaktigheten til kildene til “kunnskap”. Den hjelper oss å stille spørsmålet: “Prøver denne personen å selge meg noe? Har de virkelig vitenskapelige studier som viser at det de sier er sant?”

Dette er to spørsmål jeg stiller når jeg ser på en nettside. Er det lenker til produkter som blir solgt til meg, og er reklamen tydelig adskilt fra artiklene? Mer enn det, er det lenker til studier som støtter det som hevdes? Hvis det er, hvor store var disse studiene? Hvis en studie bare har 12 personer, er den ikke stor nok til å gi pålitelig informasjon.

Robert Harris laget akronymet CARS, som hjelper med å avgjøre om informasjon på en nettside er gyldig. Troverdighet, tidligere Nøyaktighet, Rimelighet og Støttende informasjon er alle viktige å se på for å avgjøre om vi bør verdsette informasjonen på en nettside.2

Dessverre prøver mange som hevder å ha svar på hvordan man lever lenge og sunt, faktisk å selge bøker, kosttilskudd og ulike andre produkter. En fremtredende lege som fremmer bedre helse gjennom bruk av kosttilskudd (som han selger) har klart å samle nok penger gjennom dette at han i en erklæring fra 2017 uttalte at han var verdt mer enn 100 millioner dollar. Dette betyr ikke at han ikke har noe å tilby, men det sier at han har en skjevhet i retning av å anbefale ting han selv selger.

American Medical Association har retningslinjer for leger som skal selge produkter fra sine kontorer etisk. Disse retningslinjene sier at produktene bør dekke et bestemt presserende behov (for eksempel krykker på en ortopedisk klinikk), ha vitenskapelig gyldighet for sin bruk, og at leger bør gi informasjon om andre måter pasienter kan få de samme produktene andre steder.3 Mer enn det bør leger opplyse pasientene om enhver økonomisk interesse de måtte ha i produktet som tilbys pasienten.

Bekreftelsesbias

De fleste av oss leser for å bekrefte tingene vi allerede tror. Jeg ser dette når folk leser Bibelen— på merkelig vis kan folk lese Bibelen og fullstendig ignorere Skrifter som motsier deres handlinger når det gjelder politisk engasjement eller anstendighet i klesdrakt, men likevel tro at de følger alt Skriften sier.

På samme måte kan hver av oss finne historier og informasjon som forsterker våre oppfatninger om leger og medisin. Hvis vi tror at leger kun er ute etter penger og er uetiske og foreskriver medisiner som er giftige for pasienter, kan vi finne artikler som bekrefter det. På den annen side, hvis vi søker etter historier som river ned teorier om alternativ medisin, kan vi også finne slike artikler.

Det viktige er at vi går til spørsmålet på jakt etter reelle svar og forstår at vitenskapen ikke vet alt.

Som et eksempel har vi ikke gode behandlinger for folk som har langvarige COVID-symptomer. Det betyr ikke at mange som led gjennom COVID måneder tidligere ikke lider av ting som mental tåke og tretthet, men det betyr at det ikke finnes en enkelt medisin som har gjort det bedre enn sukkerpiller i studier for å fjerne disse symptomene.

I fravær av vitenskapelig dokumenterte behandlingsplaner har mange klinikker utviklet sine egne behandlingsforløp, ved å bruke en blanding av kosttilskudd og til og med hyperbar oksygenbehandling. Er disse nyttige? Det vet jeg ikke, men jeg vet at de som markedsfører dem vil hevde med selvtillit at de har svært høy suksessrate i å kurere folk hvis de bare er villige til å følge (og betale for) behandlingsplanen.

Mer enn det, når folk forsker på symptomene sine, har de en tendens til å velge hvilke diagnoser de synes er sannsynlige basert på underliggende personlighetstyper. Noen mennesker er tilbøyelige til å katastrofetenkning— det vil si at de umiddelbart tror det verste tenkelige utfallet i enhver gitt situasjon de blir presentert for. Disse vil skrive inn symptomer og komme fram til at de har kreft og bare har dager eller uker igjen å leve. Som Gud sa til Hiskia, er det tid for dem å ordne huset sitt.

På den annen side finnes det mange mennesker med en optimistisk personlighet. De skriver inn symptomlisten og kommer fram til at de har en mild virusinfeksjon og vil føle seg bedre om noen dager.

Hensikten med å ha en medisinsk leverandør til å gjennomgå ting er at utøveren (forhåpentligvis) kan skille de sannsynlige tingene fra de usannsynlige. De har ikke det emosjonelle overbygget som pasientene har, så de kan objektivt avgjøre hvor mange tester som skal bestilles og hvilken type tester for å komme fram til en diagnose.

Leger kan identifisere farlige situasjoner

Jeg husker å ha sett en pasient for mange år siden som kom til meg med det hun trodde var en bihulebetennelse. Hun var i 20-årene og sa at hun hadde en dunkende følelse i hodet og mye trykk.

Hun hadde egentlig ikke mye sekresjon eller feber og ingen av de typiske symptomene på bihulebetennelse, men sinuitis virket som den mest sannsynlige diagnosen hun kunne komme på.

Jeg tok ett blikk på henne og likte ikke det jeg så. For det første var hun ekstremt blek. For det andre var pulsen hennes ganske rask – 130 slag i minuttet i hvile. Da jeg undersøkte henne, fant jeg ingenting som tydet på at hun hadde bihulebetennelse.

“Jenny,” sa jeg til henne. “Du må gå til sykehuset og ta en akutt blodtelling. Jeg frykter at du virkelig er anemisk— selv om jeg ikke vet hvorfor. Vent på laboratoriet, så snakker vi når jeg får resultatene.”

Det var kanskje 20 minutter senere at jeg fikk en presserende telefon fra sykehusets laboratorium. “Dr. Waldron,” sa stemmen i den andre enden. “Vi har et kritisk labsvar til deg…”

Jennys hemoglobin var 4,6 (normalt er mellom 12 og 16), og hun endte opp med å få en blodoverføring. Det hun ikke fikk, var behandling for en bihulebetennelse.

Brystsmerter er et klassisk symptom som kan peke mot en underliggende hjertetilstand. Samtidig kan det simpelthen indikere esofageal refluks (syre i spiserøret) eller betennelse i et ribbein eller en muskel. Jeg ser sannsynligvis et par pasienter hver dag som har dette symptomet.

De fleste av dem trenger enkel behandling, men noen få må sendes raskt til sykehus for en fullstendig hjerteundersøkelse. Jeg vet ikke hvordan en søkemotor på nettet skal vite hvilken retning en person bør ta etter å ha gjennomgått symptomene sine.

Høyst sannsynlig vil en nettressurs henvise en brukeren til å oppsøke akuttjenester eller sin lokale lege.

Ikke alle leger er like

Rundt 50 prosent av legene endte i den nedre halvdelen av sin medisinstudieklasse. Bare fordi noen ikke hadde toppkarakterer på medisinstudiet, betyr det ikke at de mangler tilstrekkelig kunnskap til å behandle en sykdom. Kanskje den viktigste kunnskapen en lege trenger, er å vite når han ikke vet.

Det er fortsatt utfordrende for pasienter å vite om de har med noen som faktisk vil hjelpe dem. Når du møter en lege, har du en tendens til å dømme dem basert på deres “sengekant-manner”. De fleste av oss ser etter noen som utstråler selvtillit og virker som om de vet hva de gjør.

Selvtillit er ikke det samme som kompetanse, og det finnes mange leger (og folk i andre felt) som har høy selvtillit, men som egentlig ikke er kompetente til å ta seg av situasjonen.

Her kan litt egen research hjelpe. For det første har legen din anmeldelser på nettet, og disse anmeldelsene vil gi en indikasjon på nivået av omsorg de gir pasientene. For det andre, hvis det legen din forteller virker merkelig, er det enkelt å gjøre litt forskning på tilstanden du angivelig har og se om symptomene stemmer og om behandlingen virker rimelig.

Det er viktig å innse at mennesker ikke er som kjøretøy. Det jeg mener med det er at det ikke finnes et skanneverktøy helsepersonell kan koble til som genererer alle feilkoder og så fikser de tingene som genererer kodene.

Selv om helsepersonell er sikre på diagnosen, svarer noen pasienter ikke på første eller engang andre tilgjengelige behandling. Det betyr ikke at diagnosen eller behandlingen var feil, men at mennesker ikke er kloner av hverandre og noen responderer bedre på én type behandling enn en annen.

Kanskje en dag vil vi ha genetiske tester som forteller oss med en gang hva den perfekte medisinen eller behandlingsplanen er for en gitt sykdom, men den dagen virker langt unna.

En siste ting å nevne er at gode leger ikke vil føle seg truet av at pasientene stiller spørsmål eller gjør research. Det er tider når en pasient spør meg om en ny behandling jeg ikke er kjent med, og jeg må gjøre min egen research.

Disse situasjonene er ikke opprørende for meg, men heller en læringsmulighet. “Det er jeg ikke kjent med,” sier jeg til pasienten. “La meg gjøre litt research og snakke med noen spesialister jeg stoler på, så ringer jeg deg senere denne uken og forteller hva jeg finner ut.”

Noen ganger undersøker jeg og finner at behandlingen er kostbar og ser ut til å gi blandet eller liten nytte, men noen ganger er den en forbedring i forhold til tidligere metoder. Leger må lære og justere sin praksis etter hvert som vi lærer nye ting om sykdommer og hvordan menneskekroppen reagerer på dem.

Ydmykhet er nødvendig

Jo lengre jeg praktiserer medisin, desto mindre føler jeg at jeg vet. Det er ikke fordi jeg har utviklet demens, men fordi jeg innser at det finnes mange sykdommer vi ikke har gode behandlinger for. Menneskekroppen er utrolig kompleks. Det finnes 36 billioner celler i menneskekroppen, og normalt samarbeider de alle perfekt; problemet er å finne ut hva man skal gjøre når de ikke gjør det.

Dunning–Kruger-effekten er noe som påvirker mange felt der folk med begrenset kunnskap og ferdighet kraftig overvurderer sine evner i det feltet. Studier har vist at 65 prosent av amerikanere tror de har over gjennomsnittlig IQ.4 Statistisk sett er dette ikke mulig. Femti prosent av en hvilken som helst gruppe mennesker vil ha over gjennomsnittlig IQ, og de andre 50 prosent vil være under gjennomsnittet. Slik er IQ-skalaen satt opp.

Selv om denne effekten er til stede blant leger, finnes den også hos pasienter. “Å gjøre research” er ikke det samme som å ha brukt fire år på medisinstudiet, ytterligere tre år i et residensprogram, og fortsette å holde seg à jour med utviklingen i medisin gjennom ulike etterutdanningskurs. Vi ville alle gjøre lurt i å lytte bedre og innse våre begrensninger.

Det faktum at morens fetter tok melkurt-ekstrakt og følte seg mye bedre fra lignende symptomer som dine, er interessant. Om melkurt-ekstraktet hjalp dem å bli kvitt sykdommen, om det var en placeboeffekt, eller om de uansett ville blitt bedre, uavhengig av hva de tok, er til debatt.

Sann visdom

Jeg har allerede nevnt visdom, og jeg vil avslutte med det. Sann visdom er å innse at helbredelse kommer fra Gud. Salme 103:3 sier om Gud: “Han som tilgir alle dine misgjerninger, som leger alle dine sykdommer.”

Helbredelse kommer ikke fra antibiotika eller cellegift. Den kommer ikke fra å ta de rette kosttilskuddene eller engang å spise et sunt kosthold. Helbredelse kommer fordi Gud rører ved oss, helt ned i de minste delene av våre celler og immunsystem, og gjør ting hele igjen.

Jeg tror at noen ganger virker Han gjennom medisin, men andre ganger virker Han gjennom den virksomme, inderlige bønn fra rettferdige menn og kvinner. (Jakobsbrev 5:16)

Med all vår kunnskap er det lett for oss å fylles av stolthet og tro at vi ikke trenger noen andre. Vi lever i en verden full av kunnskap og en verden hvor visdom har blitt skjøvet bak i køen.

Vi må velge kilden til vår informasjon nøye og innse at vi ikke vet alt. Kanskje grunnen til at Herrens frykt er begynnelsen på visdom, er fordi det er det første skrittet mot å legge fra seg stoltheten og innse at vi er en liten del av skapelsen. Først da kan vi ydmykt lytte, lære og ta imot helbredelse.
